question.text: Which of the following BEST represents the alpha-beta separation concept in practice?

answer.text: An active alpha portfolio combined with a separate passive beta exposure
A single index ETF held on its own
A short position in the market index

explanation.text: The Logic: Alpha and beta decisions can be separated and generated through different portfolios — an active portfolio that drives alpha plus a separate portfolio that provides the desired beta / market exposure. The workbook calls this portable alpha / alternate beta. The Trap: A single index ETF gives only beta. A short of the index gives negative beta. Cash and bonds give neither equity alpha nor equity beta. Only the combination of an alpha engine and a separate beta-exposure portfolio captures both. Note: The two legs are sized as independent decisions; the alpha portfolio is run on its own merits and the beta exposure is added separately.
